messages:
ingrid: Heads up — SCIM provisioning to Okta started returning 401s right after an envelope key rotation around 03:12 UTC. Not a full outage but several customers saw deprovision loops :grimacing:

ingrid: Relevant logs:
```
2026-03-05T03:15:02Z svc=provisioner req=abcd123 status=401 err=\"KMS decrypt failed: envelope key not found\"
2026-03-05T03:15:03Z svc=provisioner req=efgh456 status=401 err=\"invalid token signature after decrypt\"
```

ingrid: Seen for 3 tenants, all provisioning calls from the same lambda.

omar: @ingrid can you share which KMS alias was rotated and whether Secrets Manager was updated? Which region/cluster?

ingrid: Deploy note said alias/redwood/provisioner/primary -> alias/redwood/provisioner/primary-v2 at 03:12. Auth header redacted: \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED(...)\"

deploy-bot: infra/kms-rotate v2 -> success at 03:12 UTC (owner: elaine) :white_check_mark:

elaine: I rotated the envelope key and updated the rotation table. I intended to stage the secret flip but didnt switch the secret ARN yet to validate traffic first.

omar: That could explain it — if the secret still points to the old key id and the old key is disabled/deleted, decrypt fails. We should check Secrets Manager and KMS alias mapping.

security-oncall: Capture CloudTrail KMS Decrypt results and Secrets Manager events for 03:05-03:30. Need to know if Decrypt returned NotFound vs AccessDenied. Tag incident sec-2026-03-05-kms-rotate.

ruthie: Looking now. KMS aliases show both present. alias redwood/provisioner/primary -> key-id K-OLD (scheduled), alias redwood/provisioner/primary-v2 -> K-NEW. Secrets Manager secret svc/provisioner/kms_arn still contains K-OLD ARN.

elaine: Oof, I held the secret flip intentionally. I can push the new secret ARN now but worried about cached clients pinning old ARN — though our lambdas fetch secrets at cold start.

omar: Two remediation options: (A) Re-enable K-OLD decrypt permission temporarily to let flows succeed while we flip secret, or (B) update the secret immediately. Which is lower risk?

ingrid: Re-enable old key for short window seems safest to avoid any deprovision storms.

elaine: Plan: re-enable K-OLD and add CryptoDecrypt to provisioner role, push secret update with version label \"rotate-2026-03-05\", monitor for 5m, then remove K-OLD decrypt permission and schedule disable.

security-oncall: Do it and capture CloudTrail/PutSecretValue events. Also collect affected-tenant list for CS.

ruthie: Executing now: re-enabled K-OLD and patched key policy (03:23). Uploaded secret rotate-2026-03-05 with K-NEW ARN (03:26).

ingrid: Seeing provisioning return 200s again for previously failing tenants. :tada:

security-oncall: Good. Save CloudTrail snippets and create incident doc under /incidents/sec-2026-03-05-kms-rotate. We'll do full postmortem on why secrets flip was delayed and update runbooks.

elaine: Postmortem action items: add explicit 3-step checklist for envelope rotation: (1) stage new key and alias, (2) update consumer config/secret, (3) retire old key. Update oncall playbook to check Secrets Manager first on decrypt failures.

omar: I'll open a small PR to emit obfuscated decrypt key-id in provisioner logs to trace future rotations and add a unit test for decrypt failure handling.

ingrid: Filing a short customer note for CS re: duplicate deprovision attempts and mitigation.

security-oncall: Closing thread; moving artifacts to incident doc. :lock:
